Using partial fractions, we have

$$
\dfrac{1}{(n+2)(n+3)} = \dfrac{1}{n+2} - \dfrac{1}{n+3}.
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
\displaystyle \sum\limits_{n = 1}^\infty   \left(\dfrac{1}{n+2} - \dfrac{1}{n+3}\right).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{1} & =(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}) \\ {s}_{2} & =(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\frac{1}{5}) \\ {s}_{3} & =(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{6}) \\ {s}_{4} & =(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms except for the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
s_N = \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{N+3}.
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of $s_N\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(n+2)(n+3)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
